I could not derive this exponent from first principles or confirm it against the literature, so this is a best recollection.

The length of the LLF loop-erased walk is at most $n+1$, so $\alpha \le 0$. For chronological loop erasure in $\mathbb{Z}^4$, the length is of order $n(\log n)^{-1/3}$. My best recollection is that the largest-loop-first version has a more negative exponent, $-2/3$, but I have not verified this.

ANSWER: -2/3
